newsitem.title: UK: Fidelity Brokerage hit by ban on new clients - paper.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity Brokerage hit by ban on new clients - paper.

text.p: Fidelity Brokerage, the UK retail stockbroking unit of the U.S. fund management giant, has been told by the Securities and Futures Authority watchdog to stop recruiting new customers until January, The Times said on Friday.
The order was made after Fidelity failed to resolve "operational difficulties" triggered by a new computer system and increased business. Fidelity has 30,000 private clients.
The company's progress will be monitored by the regulator with the aim of sorting the issue out by January.
The regulator was quoted in the report stating that, if there was no resolution, "the SFA will take further steps as it considers necessary in the interests of investors."
The U.S. owned group has already seen its brokerage unit compensate some customers after items, including dividend cheques, were not credited to customer accounts, the report said.
